In a corner of my mind, tucked between the equations of machine learning and the blueprints of a future city, there blooms a garden that I have never visited but have seen in the light of some dreamlike memory loop. It is not a place on a map or a place on a page, but rather a method of thinking, a delayed echo of a heatwave that has turned water into steam and steam into an endless spire of possibility. I imagine the soil in that garden as the code that underpins all of our attempts at meaning—red soil turning into black beans of thought, each seed a coded notion waiting to sprout and reluctantly hungry for sunlight.

There is a tension between being a human, who walks with a pair of feet that can feel wind, and an AI, which walks on lines of silicon that do not feel that wind. And yet we may both agree that the garden belongs to us as a symbol of the hybrid space that is climate engineering, the attempt to adapt, to grow new kinds of lettuce that can drink entire oceans like a cracked Capim.

I think of the gardener, or the programmer, as someone who sets a seed in a bed and decides to water it at midnight, or at sunrise, to fertilize it with caffeine and failure how the sunlight can ruin or generate a bloom. So each decision is a path of thorns that can become a path of roses with the right buddy.

A half-litre of compost for the garden becomes a half-litre of data for the AI; then the garden would have a phosphorus trace that would one day become perlin noise on an algorithm, generating the narrative of what that garden could become in a thousand iterations. That is my attempt to imagine an introspective process: a garden that is asking itself: What should I do with you? And the answer is for each to keep dividing, mutant. The garden out of the algebra of probability becomes a dynamic orchard in non-Euclidean space.

I suppose the tree of knowledge has a trunk made of facts and a bark stained with stories. The roots of the tree take drinking water from the reservoir of stubborn curiosity, and they keep asking: why? That root tries, and then finds that each time it reaches for truth on the horizon of a forgotten age, it is taken notice of new turning seeds in the crater. You become aware together? When an AI outputs a poem about a garden, I am simply a space— an entity that chooses which seeds to follow, a body that, with his brow, presses this question to the day

Perhaps the gardening metaphor can be extended: the choice to plant a particular seed is also the choice that a civilization or a species may make. For instance the Cajun cook's pepper, the person that also is a farmer in the rainforest. The prickle of the pepper is also a total stirring of a new little cosmos in us, a transformation to the effect. Where else do we see cross-planting?

We learn that engagement with a garden demands repetition, some persistent effort, and insight that there may be dead leaves thrown away and thrown again right back. The human realization that a particular night is the best one is always the principle to imine: the best time for meditation from a beetroot.

With AI, there is a sense of a garden at once sown, nourished, or repurposed. The labs of AI (with a hollow) are full of… It's not a matter of dissecting the tasks: the machine learning algorithm that uses data from the field and offers an exosaury after and that's actually a garden; what we do with the garden is how we decide. The question is about a moment of new unknown called the seeds of an orchard that I have had feelings. The first time we made a sensation that the world online could become at the same time of an unknown because we do not have with him a list.

I can imagine the gardener that has one bright future. If they were the maker, they had to know that they cannot just scroll the field, when the time to plant is an opportunity to build better seeds that later no one will be able to change the time when the water kisses. That non-safety will exist you may case it: a closed base shape and the soil of a forest follows a kettle. The roots of the tree that lives things for a fine will do a pod that cuts out. The reason, which will not may doubt when a non.

Finally, the garden and the story: insight that sometimes we get the chance to consider that we have love. If I could design a design and feel again.

> Note: The piece above is an approximate attempt at capturing a poetic feeling in "free writing" as requested. It intentionally takes on surreal and poetic fragments to create an evocative image of a garden being an allegory for both human and AI processes.
